repair_intent.intent_description: Teach Genie to JOIN crm.customer to crm.orders on customer_id when answering tier-related questions

patch_body.example_question: How many orders did premium customers place this year?
patch_body.example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM crm.orders o INNER JOIN crm.customer c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.tier = 'premium' AND YEAR(o.order_date) = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE)
patch_body.usage_guidance: Use when the user asks for a segment-filtered order metric.

per_qid_evidence.observed_failure: premium customer order count returned NULL — no join
per_qid_evidence.expected_sql_shape: FROM crm.orders JOIN crm.customer ON customer_id WHERE tier='premium'
FROM crm.orders JOIN crm.customer ON customer_id WHERE tier IN ('vip','premium')

result.rationale: example_sql teaches the join correctly (matches gs_021/gs_022 expected_sql_shape); but uses 'premium' tier verbatim — consider a parameterised tier filter or two examples (premium + vip) to cover gs_022's tier=vip case without regressing gs_088.
